messages.author: 6db3c86d422c5ae9
messages.subject: modindices() not include intercept
parts:
Hi,

I am studying measurement invariance using lavaan package. When I run command modindices() for the strong model I found no information on intercepts (~1).
I am now using the lastest version of lavaan which is 0.5-20. Does anyone know how to solve this problem?

Thank you very much,
Kind regards,
Tuan

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: modindices() not include intercept
parts:
For equality constrained parameters, use the lavTestScore() function.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: modindices() not include intercept
parts:
First, look at the parameter table of your model:

parTable(model3)

At the bottom, you will see the 'equality' contraints. Each '.p?.' label
refers to a parameter.

Then, first section of the output of lavTestScore() is the 'global'
(multivariate) score test: what happens if we release all equality
constraints together. Next, you will see the 'univariate' score tests:
what happens if we release one constraint at a time. These are the
modification indices you are looking for.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: modindices() not include intercept
parts:
On 06/09/2016 10:03 AM, Ba Tuan Vu wrote:
> Dear Prof. Yves,
>
> I found that parameters from number 25 to number 33 refer to .p25 to
> .p33. They are indicators for intercept. It seems that .p27 (x3) and
> .p31 (x7) are non-invariant across groups (and therefore they should be
> free). Is this explanation correct?

These are univariate tests, so should check this one by one. Fit a model
where you free one intercept constraint (say, for x3). Then, run this
lavTestScore() function again. It may be that the results are already
different.

> In addition I don't understand some
> other parameters that is on "rhs" column. Could you please tell me what
> the column refers to?

The are most likely similar parameters but in the second group.

Yves.
